verdicts.reason: Arithmetic is exact, not approximate: I re-measured all three universes and 445 + 2,120 + 13,370 = 15,935 holds (SODA i9wp-a4ja count = 2,120; 39hk-dx4f = 496 rows / 445 distinct complex_id; the archived static zips give per-feed 1,884/4,558/2,732/1,825/1,398/1,940, sum 14,337, union 13,370 distinct stop_id). ref/ is also the right layer: 01 already names `ref/assets` as the anti-join left side, and a frozen external snapshot matches the ref/grids and ref/picks precedent. Four things break. (a) The sentence 'Cell-grain scoring does NOT get asset rows' contradicts 01's resolved negative generator, which is literally 'ref/assets x flood_events LEFT ANTI JOIN flood_labels'. If Cell is a published score unit (D3 says it is) and cells are not rows in ref/assets, cell-grain negatives have no generator, and gold/flood_labels — keyed on asset_id — would carry cell rows with a NULL asset_id, i.e. two grains and a nullable key in one table. (b) The geometry column is called `geom`; 09's schemas name it `geometry` on every geometry table (cells, zones, stops, shapes) and the flood map's Notes say pipeline-09 storage is reused wholesale, no re-deciding. (c) `structure` is a station attribute, not a complex attribute: I measured 9 of 445 complexes carrying more than one distinct structure across their stations (4 Av-9 St Subway/Viaduct; Broadway Junction, Myrtle-Wyckoff Avs, Franklin Av, 161 St-Yankee Stadium, Jackson Hts-Roosevelt Av, Court Sq-23 St all Elevated/Subway; Botanic Garden and 62 St Open Cut/Subway). No collapse rule is given. (d) `feeds` as a 'pipe-list' hand-rolls an encoding Parquet has natively, against 09's typing conventions.
verdicts.amendment:
D1 One table, physical point assets only

`ref/assets` at `data/ref/assets/` — one GeoParquet 1.1 file, Sedona-written with SRID 4326 so `crs` is omitted, sorted (kind, asset_id), exactly 15,935 rows = 445 complexes + 2,120 entrances + 13,370 bus stops (all three counts measured 2026-08-22, not estimated). Typed columns:

| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| asset_id | STRING pk | per D2 |
| kind | STRING | complex / entrance / bus_stop |
| geometry | POINT (GeoParquet, DOUBLE bbox) | SRID 4326, lon/lat |
| lon, lat | DOUBLE | as published by the source |
| cell | INT64 | h3(point, res 8); hex string at any JSON boundary (09) |
| complex_id | STRING | complex + entrance rows; NULL on bus_stop |
| parent_asset_id | STRING | entrance -> its complex; NULL otherwise |
| gtfs_stop_id | ARRAY<STRING> | subway stop ids on complex rows (02's attachment path); source publishes 3 multi-valued entrance rows semicolon-delimited ('718; R09', 'A12; D13', 'A32; D20') — split at ingest |
| structure | ARRAY<STRING> | distinct `structure` values over the complex's stations, sorted; 9 of 445 complexes carry two (measured) |
| entrance_type | STRING | entrance rows; exact published literals, e.g. 'Easement - Street' (spaced hyphen), not 'Easement-Street' |
| entry_allowed, exit_allowed | BOOL | entrance rows; YES 2,072 / NO 48 measured on entry_allowed |
| feeds | ARRAY<STRING> | bus_stop rows, sorted feed names |
| pick_id | ARRAY<STRING> | bus_stop rows, the sha1s behind `feeds` (D6) |
| parent_suspect | BOOL | entrance rows failing D5's 300 m parent gate |
| first_seen_date | DATE | D6 |

Cells stay out of this table (they are ref/cells, and a polygon grain in a point table buys nothing), but the consequence must be written down rather than assumed: the negatives generator 01 specifies is amended to `(ref/assets UNION ALL ref/cells) x flood_events LEFT ANTI JOIN flood_labels`, with a comment left on ticket 01. Cell-support label rows carry asset_id = `cell:<h3 hex>` so asset_id stays non-null and single-typed across gold/flood_labels.

verdicts.reason: The entrance key collides on real data. I fetched all 2,120 rows: (complex_id, entrance_latitude, entrance_longitude) at full published precision is unique 2,120/2,120, exactly as the draft says — but the key hashes a DIFFERENT tuple. (complex_id, round(lat,3), lon) yields only 2,118 distinct values. Two named collisions: complex 614 (59 St-Columbus Circle) rows 40.7693477 and 40.7692671 sharing lon -73.9823068, and complex 429 (Freeman St) rows 40.8304069 and 40.8299244 sharing lon -73.8920048. Rounding latitude to 3 dp is ~111 m of tolerance and it was never the thing measured unique; two entrances silently merge into one asset_id. Separately, three bus-stop facts are wrong or arbitrary. The pair arithmetic does not close: 967 is the extra-instance count (14,337 - 13,370), not a pair count. Measured feed multiplicity is 909 ids in 2 feeds, 21 in 3, 4 in 4, 1 in 5, which is 1,006 pairwise pairs, not 967. 'max 0.1 km' is understated — measured max is 147.7 m, and it is 3 pairs at or above 100 m (that count is right, its denominator is not). And 'coords from the lexicographically-first feed' is an arbitrary tiebreak with a measured consequence: 14 of the 935 shared stop_ids land in a DIFFERENT H3 res-8 cell depending on which feed wins, silently changing which precip Cell-hour those assets join to; a 147.7 m displacement also exceeds 01's RADIUS_M = 100 m outright, so the attachment set for that asset can be wholly disjoint.
verdicts.amendment:
D2 Keys

- complex: `stn:<complex_id>` (445)
- entrance: `ent:<complex_id>:<sha1(lat_str + ',' + lon_str)|8>` where lat_str/lon_str are the `entrance_latitude`/`entrance_longitude` strings EXACTLY as `i9wp-a4ja` publishes them (3-8 decimal places, no reformatting, no rounding). That is the tuple measured unique at 2,120/2,120; rounding latitude to 3 dp collides two pairs (complex 614 59 St-Columbus Circle; complex 429 Freeman St) and is rejected. Test: 2,120 distinct entrance asset_ids.
- bus stop: `bus:<stop_id>` — stop_id is a valid global key (measured: 935 shared ids, 1,006 cross-feed pairs, median 9.8 m apart, 191 pairs coordinate-identical, max 147.7 m, 3 pairs >= 100 m). Coordinates for a shared id are the arithmetic mean of the feeds' coordinates, not a feed-order pick: the mean is order-free and cannot be moved by adding a feed, whereas 'lexicographically first' flips the H3 res-8 cell for 14 of the 935 shared ids and can displace an asset by 147.7 m — more than 01's RADIUS_M. `feeds` and `pick_id` record every source. Test: the 3 pairs >= 100 m are listed in the build log.

verdicts.reason: Two collisions with how 01 and 02 actually attach labels. First, the citation is wrong. D3 says 'complex (subway — alert labels land here per 02)'. 01's resolved Attachment paragraph reads 'alert station -> GTFS stop_id -> complex_id -> entrances directly, no radius, rows carry label_support=station', and 02's Answer repeats 'entrances join on complex_id per 01'. Under the resolved rule the alert label lands on ENTRANCE asset_ids with station-grain support; neither ticket puts it on a complex asset_id. D3 asserts the opposite and cites the ticket that says otherwise. Second and harder: 01's label_support enum is {entrance, station, cell} and D1's kind set is {complex, entrance, bus_stop}. Bus stops have NO label_support member at all, yet they are 84% of the registry (13,370 of 15,935) and a declared published score unit. Any 311 / HWM / FloodNet point attaching to a bus stop within RADIUS_M has no legal label_support value to write. 'complex' vs 'station' is a second naming mismatch in the same enum. Third, D3 makes the complex a score unit and entrances the label carriers but never defines the roll-up, so the complex's own label is undefined. Fourth, unstated consequence: with entrances excluded as score units, bus_stop — the largest unit — has exactly one dense label channel (311 SJ/SH within 100 m) plus Sandy contains, HWMs and FloodNet; no alert path, no station path.
verdicts.amendment:
D3 Scoring units vs feature carriers

Published score units: complex (subway), bus_stop, and Cell. Entrances are feature carriers and display detail, not separately-headlined scores. Three attachment rules, which amend 01 and get a comment left on that ticket:

1. label_support becomes {entrance, station, bus_stop, cell}. 'station' keeps its 01 meaning (evidence names a station, no radius) and its asset_id is the complex row `stn:<complex_id>`; 'bus_stop' is new and is required — 01's three-value enum has no legal value for the 84% of assets that are bus stops.
2. Alert labels write ONE row per (complex, event) at asset_id = `stn:<complex_id>`, label_support='station' — not one row per entrance. This is the change to 01's 'entrances directly' chain; it is also 4.8x fewer rows (measured mean 4.8 entrances per complex) and it matches the score unit. 02's delivered path (matched alias -> station rows -> complex_id) is unchanged and terminates one step earlier.
3. Complex rows are EXCLUDED from radius attachment (see D5 — the centroid is a fiction). A complex's point-source label is the OR over its entrance rows' labels within the event window, computed at read; the entrance rows themselves carry label_support='entrance'.

Stated plainly for 08: bus_stop labels come from 311 SJ/SH at 100 m, Sandy contains, HWMs and FloodNet only — no alert or station channel reaches a bus stop, so 84% of the asset universe is trained against the dense-but-noisy tier. 08 reports bus_stop CSI separately from complex CSI; pooling them pools two different label regimes. Final call on the published units stays with 08.

verdicts.reason: The decision itself survives and the asset-count argument is better than the draft claims: I counted NYC's street centerline live — `inkn-q76z` returns 122,256 segments — so '~100K+' is right and should carry the measured number instead of a tilde. But the rationale's load-bearing clause is false as of the map's current state. '311 (the only street-grain label source)' contradicts the flood map's own Not-yet-specified list, which parks 'Bus flood alerts (665+472 route-grain rows) as a segment-grain label source — only if segment labels starve after 06 decides segments.' D4 IS that decision. Collapsing to Cell means segment labels can never starve, so the trigger on that fog item can never fire and it dangles resolved-by-omission. 01 rejected bus alerts as labels for the label table and explicitly deferred the segment question here; 06 has to close it, not restate a premise 01 already qualified.
verdicts.amendment:
D4 Street segments: collapsed to Cell for v1

LION/CSCL is not ingested. Rationale: the street-grain label sources are 311 SJ/SH (which attaches spatially at 100 m to points and Cells identically) and, as the only segment-native candidate, the 665+472 route-grain bus flood alerts that 01 rejected for lacking point geometry. Segments would add 122,256 assets (measured: NYC street centerline `inkn-q76z`, 2026-08-22) — 7.7x the entire point registry — plus a line-geometry pipeline, for one label source that is already fully served at Cell grain.

This closes the map's parked item 'Bus flood alerts as a segment-grain label source — only if segment labels starve after 06 decides segments': with no segment grain there is nothing to starve, so the bus-alert revisit is retired for v1, not left pending. Revisit trigger (fog) is restated on the Cell: a consumer needs street-level display, or 08 measures Cell-grain CSI against FloodNet point truth and finds the grain too coarse. Only that reopens both segments and the bus-alert source together.

verdicts.reason: Cell assignment mechanics are right and match 09/14 (Sedona writes, DuckDB h3 as test oracle). I also verified the assumption the draft never states: computing h3 res 8 for all 2,120 entrances, all 445 complex centroids and all 13,370 bus-stop points, every single one lands inside the 4,113-cell ref/cells footprint — good news that should be an assertion, because 09 defines the precip footprint per src as exactly the cell_pixel Pixel set derived from ref/cells, so an out-of-footprint asset would silently get no precip features at all. Three things are wrong. (a) 'A complex whose entrances span two Cells is fine' is measurably understated: 79 of 445 complexes span more than one cell (71 span two, 8 span three), and 8 complexes have a centroid Cell containing NONE of their own entrances — for those the precip feature is drawn from a cell where the complex has no physical presence. (b) 'labels attach by radius/station path' hand-waves the case that matters. Measured centroid-to-entrance distances: median-nearest 31 m, median-farthest 85 m, p90-farthest 159 m, max 3,159 m; 162 of 445 complexes have at least one entrance beyond RADIUS_M = 100 m from the centroid, and 19 complexes have no entrance at all within 100 m of their centroid. A 311 report standing on a complex's stairs can therefore fail to attach to that complex. The draft never says whether complex rows are radius-eligible. (c) parent_asset_id is built from complex_id with no sanity gate, and the source has errors: 11 entrance rows (0.52%) sit more than 300 m from every station of their assigned complex, up to 3,159 m. Named cases — complex 602 (14 St-Union Sq) holds one entrance whose own stop_name is '34 St-Herald Sq' while complex 607 (34 St-Herald Sq) holds four named '14 St-Union Sq' (a straight swap), and four '61 St-Woodside' entrances are parented to the 7-line complexes 458/459/460/461. D3's 'min entrance DEM, worst freeboard' roll-up would take its minimum over an entrance 3 km away.
verdicts.amendment:
D5 Cell assignment and complex geometry

Every asset row carries cell = h3(point, res 8), computed at build with Spark/Sedona, DuckDB h3 as test oracle (09/14). Build assertion, not an assumption: every asset's cell is in `ref/cells` — measured 15,935/15,935 today; an asset outside the 4,113-cell footprint gets no precip features at all, since 09 defines the per-src precip footprint as the cell_pixel Pixel set derived from ref/cells.

Complex point = centroid of its constituent stations' gtfs lat/lon (496 stations -> 445 complexes). The centroid is a FICTION and is used for exactly one thing: the complex's precip-feature Cell join. Complex rows are excluded from radius attachment entirely (measured: 162 of 445 complexes have an entrance beyond 100 m of the centroid, and 19 have no entrance within 100 m of it — a report standing on the stairs would miss). Complex point labels come from the station path (D3) plus the OR over its entrance rows.

Multi-cell complexes are named, not waved past: 79 of 445 span more than one Cell (71 two, 8 three), and 8 complexes have a centroid Cell containing none of their own entrances. Those 8 carry `cell_suspect = true` and 08 reads their precip features from the modal entrance Cell instead.

Parent gate: an entrance is parented to its complex_id only if it lies within 300 m of that complex's nearest station. Measured distribution p50 58 m, p90 115 m, p99 204 m, then a clean break — nothing between 300 m and 875 m — and 11 rows (0.52%) beyond it, all source errors (complexes 602/607 have entrance rows swapped; four '61 St-Woodside' entrances are parented to 458/459/460/461). Those 11 keep their row but get `parent_suspect = true`, are excluded from the complex's D3 roll-up and from 07's min-entrance aggregates, and are listed in the build log.

verdicts.reason: The frozen-snapshot shape is right and matches the ref/grids frozen_at precedent, and the pick dates check out against the archive (bronx/brooklyn/busco/manhattan/queens all 2026-06-23, staten_island 2026-07-28 — the only zip per feed the archiver holds, so there is no version choice to make). Three problems. (a) Rail violation: bus picks are named by zip DATE, but 09 and 12 identify a Pick by `pick_id` = sha1 of the zip bytes — that is ref/picks' primary key and the partition key on every schedule table. A date is not a pick identity. (b) Reproducibility hole: 01 defines label_version = sha1(311 as-of, alert as-of, frozen thresholds, RADIUS_M). The registry is not in that hash, yet 01 generates the entire negative class by anti-joining ref/assets. Swap the registry and every label set silently changes with an unchanged label_version. (c) The existence framing is refuted by 01's own estimand. 01 names the target `flooded_reported` = P(a report/detection is generated), stated plainly, not P(asset floods). Under that estimand 'inherits its location's earlier flood history — correct for exposure-of-the-location' does not hold: no report could be generated at a station that did not exist. Worse, the draft only flags the negative-side bias; the positive side is the sharper error, because 01 attaches Sandy 2012 polygons by `contains` and USGS HWMs as label-grade, so post-2012 assets (Second Av Sub 2017, Hudson Yards 2015, the reopened Cortlandt St 2018) will be minted as 2012 POSITIVES. Fabricated positives are worse than biased negatives, and the fix is one nullable column, not validity windows.
verdicts.amendment:
D6 Versioning and asset existence

ref/assets is a frozen snapshot carrying `frozen_at TS` plus per-source as-of provenance. Bus picks are identified by `pick_id` = sha1 of the zip bytes (09/12; a date is not a pick identity), recorded per feed on the bus_stop rows: bronx 1e05b66603f781491ba2f9e6c3a012ed68e599f3 (2026-06-23), brooklyn c05b9aefc277ec4e766c07ea5ea9c26faa7bcbfc (2026-06-23), busco 3d84ded191bcc80d82a6653655b1064fc495bb6a (2026-06-23), manhattan e19457c845680d939472dfb801c1a35bed1479fd (2026-06-23), queens 1382a2eba797e7257b197a360e0396ac5e2ed812 (2026-06-23), staten_island 2df7eee4c96825d3418ba604958122875c6182ea (2026-07-28 — the only feed on a later pick). Subway sources carry their Socrata as-of stamps.

`asset_version` = sha1 of (the two Socrata as-of stamps, the six pick_ids in feed order, the D2 key rule, the D5 parent-gate metres). It MUST enter 01's label_version alongside the 311/alert as-ofs, thresholds and RADIUS_M, because 01 generates the whole negative class by anti-joining ref/assets — comment left on ticket 01. Re-freezing rebuilds the table whole (09: ref/ tables are rebuilt whole) and bumps asset_version; note that a corrected upstream coordinate changes an entrance's asset_id, so a re-freeze invalidates stored label rows keyed on it — labels are regenerated, never migrated.

Asset existence: each row carries `first_seen_date DATE` (Socrata as-of for subway, minus a hand-list of the ~10 complexes opened after 2012-10-29 — Second Av Sub 2017, Hudson Yards 2015, Cortlandt St reopened 2018, the 7 line extension; pick as-of for bus stops). Asset x event rows where the event window ends before first_seen_date are excluded from POSITIVES first and from anti-join negatives second. This is required, not optional: 01's estimand is `flooded_reported` = P(a report is generated), and no report can be generated at an asset that does not exist — without the cut, 01's Sandy-polygon `contains` attachment and the 2012 HWMs mint fabricated 2012 positives for assets built in 2015-2018. One nullable column plus one WHERE clause; per-asset validity windows stay out unless 08's per-event diagnostics demand them.

missing: Typed physical schema. The draft names columns but no types, no path, no sort key, no partition, no file count, and never states the SRID-4326/crs-omitted rule. Every resolved pipeline ticket shipped a typed schema into research/09-storage-schemas.md; 06 must do the same (`data/ref/assets/`, one GeoParquet 1.1 file, sorted (kind, asset_id)).

asset_version and its propagation into 01's label_version. The negative class is generated by anti-joining ref/assets, so the registry is a label input; 01's sha1 does not cover it and no comment is proposed back to 01.

label_support has no member for bus stops. 01's enum is {entrance, station, cell}; D1 creates a bus_stop kind that is 84% of the registry and a declared score unit. Any 311/HWM/FloodNet point attaching to a bus stop has no legal support value. Also unresolved: 'station' (01) vs 'complex' (D1) naming for the same asset.

Whether complex rows participate in 100 m radius attachment at all, and the entrance-to-complex label roll-up rule (OR within the event window). Measured: 19 of 445 complexes have NO entrance within 100 m of their centroid, so radius attachment on a complex point is not merely imprecise, it can be empty.

How cell-grain negatives are generated. 01's anti-join names ref/assets only; D1 keeps cells out of ref/assets while D3 makes Cell a published score unit. The generator has to be restated as (ref/assets UNION ref/cells) x flood_events, or cells get asset rows.

A station-to-complex lookup. 02's delivered path is matched alias -> station rows -> complex_id, and the registry stores no gtfs_stop_id anywhere. The entrance table cannot substitute: measured, 14 station gtfs_stop_ids never appear on any entrance row, 8 station_ids have no entrance row, and 3 entrance gtfs_stop_id values are semicolon-multi-valued ('718; R09', 'A12; D13', 'A32; D20').

Bus-stop inclusion rule. 'union 13,370 distinct stop_ids' states no filter. All six feeds are location_type=0 only (measured), so there are no GTFS station/entrance rows to exclude — but whether stops with no trip in the pick are kept, and whether a future pick could carry a stop outside the ref/cells footprint, are undecided.

A non-arbitrary cross-feed coordinate rule plus its test. 'Lexicographically-first feed' flips the H3 res-8 cell for 14 of the 935 shared stop_ids (measured) and can move an asset 147.7 m — more than RADIUS_M.

What happens to the 11 mis-parented entrance rows (>300 m from every station of their complex, max 3,159 m): drop, flag, or repair. Without a rule they poison 07's min-entrance DEM and worst-freeboard roll-ups.

A null/zero-coordinate rule. 01 dropped 311 rows with null/(0,0) coordinates and reported the fraction; the registry needs the same standing assertion (measured today: 0 missing and 0 zero across all 2,120 entrances, but that is a fact about one snapshot, not a rule).

A build assertion that every asset's cell is in ref/cells. Measured 15,935/15,935 today; without the assertion an out-of-footprint asset silently gets no precip features, since 09 derives the per-src precip footprint from ref/cells via cell_pixel.

The runnable checks. Repo convention is one named test per slice (09's sum(weight)=1, the Times Square axis gate, 14's ST_Equals h3 oracle); the draft names none. Minimum set: asset_id uniqueness = 15,935; entrance-key uniqueness = 2,120; the 445<->445 complex join with zero orphans; cell membership in ref/cells; GeoParquet written with `crs` omitted.

Label fan-out from the chosen asset density, which is 06's consequence to own. Measured within RADIUS_M = 100 m: a bus stop has a mean 1.8 other bus stops (p90 4, max 17) and an entrance has a mean 3.7 other entrances (p90 7, max 17) — so one 311 point mints ~2.8 bus-stop and ~4.7 entrance positives that are perfectly correlated. 01 clusters errors by event only; asset-level correlation from a single report is unaddressed.

Sizing of the negative class. 15,935 assets x the (unbuilt) event spine is the cross product 08 consumes; no row estimate or storage shape is given, and no statement of whether negatives are materialised or generated at read.

SIR scope. Measured 21 SIR complexes / 66 entrance rows in the source, and 02's top stations include Richmond Valley SIR, so the alert path reaches them — but the draft never states whether SIR complexes are in-scope score units or how their non-subway-GTFS stop_ids resolve.

Exact source literals. entrance_type is transcribed as 'Easement-Street' / 'Easement-Passage'; the published values are 'Easement - Street' / 'Easement - Passage' with spaced hyphens. 01 made exact literals a rule (never LIKE) after the street-light miss, so this is a rail, not a typo. `exit_allowed` also exists alongside `entry_allowed` and is silently dropped with no reason given.

verdicts.reason: Three faults. (a) The Cell carve-out breaks 01: negatives are defined there as `ref/assets x flood_events LEFT ANTI JOIN flood_labels`, and flood_labels carries a single STRING asset_id plus label_support='cell'. With no Cell rows in ref/assets, cell-grain negatives come from nowhere and asset_id for cell rows is undefined (a builder must invent either a second anti-join or a null asset_id). 4,113 Cell rows cost 26% more rows in a 16K-row static table and delete a branch at every consumer — that is the lazier side. (b) Dead columns: parent_asset_id is literally 'stn:'||complex_id (derive it); `feeds` is a pipe-delimited list in a Parquet column with no named consumer, while ref/picks already exists (7 rows, built by ticket 02) and carries feed/published/path; entry_allowed has no consumer — measured (entry,exit) = (YES,YES) 2065, (NO,YES) 48, (YES,NO) 7, so the 48 'NO' rows are exit-only stairs, physically identical holes, and D3's 'open-stair count' is entrance_type='Stair' regardless. (c) One column is missing that every consumer needs: no name/stop_name anywhere, so 14's serving panel and every debug query must re-join two Socrata snapshots and six zips to print a label. (d) `structure` is a per-station field stored on a complex row: 9 of 445 complexes mix structures (608 Subway/Viaduct; 604/616/606/621/627/630 Elevated+Subway; 615 Elevated/Open Cut; 626 Open Cut/Subway) and the collapse rule is unwritten. Also: literal values are 'Easement - Street' / 'Easement - Passage' with spaces around the hyphen, not the draft's 'Easement-Street'.
verdicts.amendment:
## D1 One table, one point per asset

`ref/assets` — one GeoParquet 1.1 file (SRID 4326, crs omitted, geometry_types ["Point"]), **20,048 rows** = 445 complexes + 2,120 entrances + 13,370 bus stops + **4,113 Cells**, sorted by asset_id, single part file (the ref layer's byte-identical-rebuild gate, build ticket 02).

Columns: `asset_id` STRING pk, `kind` STRING {complex, entrance, bus_stop, cell}, `name` STRING (complex = 39hk-dx4f stop_name; bus = stops.txt stop_name; entrance = its complex's name; cell = null), `geom` POINT, `cell` INT64 (H3 res 8 of the point; for kind='cell' the identity, geom = ref/cells.centroid_lon/lat), `complex_id` STRING (complex + entrance rows), `entrance_type` STRING (entrances; 13 distinct values, note the literal spacing 'Easement - Street'), `structure` STRING (complex rows), `src_asof` DATE, `pick_id` STRING (bus rows -> ref/picks).

`structure` on a multi-structure complex (9 of 445) = the most-underground of its stations on the fixed ordinal Subway < Open Cut < Embankment < At Grade < Viaduct < Elevated — flood exposure is set by the lowest platform.

Cell rows are score units (D3), not decoration: they make the 01 anti-join one query over one table with one asset_id namespace. Polygon geometry for Cells still comes from ref/cells at serving (pipeline 14's existing rule), so nothing here duplicates it.

Dropped from the draft: `parent_asset_id` ('stn:'||complex_id — derive it), `feeds` (provenance is `pick_id` into ref/picks), `entry_allowed` (no consumer; the 48 exit-only rows stay as rows).

verdicts.reason: The entrance key is both under-specified and wrong. `sha1(lat3,lon)|8` never defines the formatted string, the rounding, the separator or the encoding — and on the obvious reading (lat rounded to 3 dp), (complex_id, round(lat,3), lon) is NOT unique: it collides on 2 rows. Source coordinates carry 1 to 8 decimal places, so formatting must be pinned. Worse, the key is built on `complex_id`, a field measured dirty: 10 of 2,120 entrance rows carry a complex_id that disagrees with the complex their gtfs_stop_id belongs to (5 x '61 St-Woodside' filed under complexes 457-461, 4 x '14 St-Union Sq' under 607, 1 x '34 St-Herald Sq' under 602) — those rows would key AND parent to a complex 1.5-3.2 km away. The draft's '445<->445, zero orphans' is a set-level check that cannot see per-row misfiling. Also unmeasured by the draft: `station_id` is not a key in 39hk-dx4f (493 distinct in 496 rows: 151, 167, 461 each name two stops), while `gtfs_stop_id` is unique — and 14 entrance rows carry a compound gtfs_stop_id ('A32; D20', 'A12; D13', '718; R09') that fails a naive join. On buses, 'coords from the lexicographically-first feed' leaves the other fields unspecified: 220 of the 935 shared stop_ids have a different stop_name across feeds, so a field-by-field merge invents a stop that exists in no feed. And the measured max cross-feed divergence is 148 m, not the draft's '0.1 km' — 3 pairs exceed RADIUS_M, so the tie-break does change label attachment for those.
verdicts.amendment:
## D2 Keys

- complex: `stn:<complex_id>` (445)
- Cell: `cell:<cell>` (4,113; `cell` is the INT64 H3 index, matching ref/cells)
- entrance: `ent:<complex_id>:<lat>:<lon>`, lat/lon formatted `%.6f` from the source strings. Measured unique over all 2,120 rows at 6 and at 5 decimals. No hash: there is nothing to shorten or hide, and a hex key cannot be eyeballed against a map. (For the record the draft's key is not unique either — (complex_id, round(lat,3), lon) collides on 2 rows.)
- **complex_id on an entrance row comes from the stations join, not from the row's own field**: split `gtfs_stop_id` on ';' (14 rows are compound; both tokens resolve to the same complex), join the first token to `39hk-dx4f.gtfs_stop_id` (unique, 496 — `station_id` is not: 151/167/461 each name two stops). Measured: 2,120/2,120 join after the split, and 10 rows get corrected off a wrong own-complex_id.
- bus stop: `bus:<stop_id>`. Where a stop_id appears in >1 feed (935 of 13,370), take the **whole row** from `min(feed)` alphabetically — geom, name and pick_id from that one row, never merged field-by-field (220 of the 935 disagree on stop_name). Measured coordinate divergence p50 10 m, p90 30 m, **max 148 m**; 3 pairs exceed the 100 m attachment radius, named as a known wobble, not fixed.
- stops.txt in all six feeds contains only platform-grain rows (location_type '0' in five feeds, empty in busco; zero location_type=1). No parent-station filter is needed — take stops.txt wholesale.

verdicts.reason: D3 names the units correctly but leaves the one rule that changes label counts unwritten: how a 311/HWM/FloodNet point becomes a positive for a complex. Read literally against 01 ('one constant RADIUS_M = 100 m, identical for every point source') the complex's own point gets the circle — and the measured geometry says that is badly wrong. After correcting the 10 misfiled rows, 24.4% of entrances sit more than 100 m from their complex's station centroid, p99 251 m, max 875 m, and **19 of 445 complexes have no entrance at all inside their own 100 m circle**. A complex-point-only rule silently drops a quarter of the actual doorways; an entrance-centroid point barely helps (19.8% / 15 complexes). Second gap: 01's `label_support` enum is {entrance, station, cell} and has no value for a bus_stop row, which is a radius-attached point exactly like an entrance. Third, D3's closing sentence ('final call belongs to 08') defers a decision 06 must make, since 07 and 08 are both blocked on 06.
verdicts.amendment:
## D3 Scoring units vs feature carriers

Published score units: **complex**, **bus_stop**, **Cell**. Entrances are feature carriers and display detail, never separately headlined.

Roll-up rule (binding, not 08's to revisit): **a complex is positive for an event iff any entrance row it parents is positive.** Point labels attach at entrance grain by the 100 m geodesic radius and OR up to `stn:<complex_id>`; the complex's own point is never used for label attachment, only for the precip-Cell join and display. Measured reason: 24.4% of entrances lie >100 m from their complex's station centroid (p99 251 m, max 875 m) and 19 of 445 complexes have zero entrances inside their own circle, so a complex-point rule would discard a quarter of the doorways. 07's entrance aggregates (min entrance DEM, worst freeboard, open-stair count) roll up on the same parent link.

`label_support` becomes {**radius**, **station**, **cell**} — the attachment method, not the asset kind (kind already lives on ref/assets): radius = any point asset inside RADIUS_M (entrance or bus stop), station = 02's alert name path, cell = H3 equality. Propagate the rename into 01's Answer; the draft's 'entrance' value has no legal value for the 13,370 bus stops.

verdicts.reason: Correct lazy call and the rationale is the real one: LION adds ~100K+ assets and a geometry pipeline for zero new label sources, because 311 — the only street-grain source — attaches at 100 m to points and Cells identically. The revisit trigger is named and falsifiable (a display consumer, or 08 measuring Cell-grain CSI against FloodNet point truth), and map.md already carries the matching fog entry for bus flood alerts as segment-grain labels. Nothing to add; with D1 amended, Cells are real asset rows, which is what a collapsed segment grain needs to be scoreable at all.

Three things a builder must invent. (a) Tooling: 'Spark/Sedona writes, DuckDB h3 as test oracle' describes the convention but not the place. The ref layer is already one file — `src/raincheck/ref.py`, `build(root, spark)` plus one builder per table, run by `make ref`, tested by `tests/test_ref.py`, with ref/cells built via `ST_H3CellIDs` and the DuckDB h3 oracle needing `ST_ReducePrecision(g, 1e-9)` on both sides. A 16K-row static table does not get a second job or a new module. (b) The complex-point choice is presented as if it mattered; measured, it does not — station-centroid vs entrance-centroid differ p50 26 m, p90 81 m, max 161 m. Keep the cheaper one and say the choice is cosmetic, so nobody re-litigates it. (c) Unstated risk with a one-line guard: `ref/cells` is `ST_H3CellIDs(bbox, 8, fullCover=false)` = 4,113 fully-covered Cells; `true` would give 4,472. A point inside the bbox but in one of the 359 rim Cells gets an H3 index that is not in ref/cells, and its precip join then returns nothing silently (no cell_pixel weights). Measured clean today — the nearest of all 16,457 source points is 0.0164 deg from the bbox edge and one H3-8 cell spans ~0.0106 deg lat — but the archiver adds picks daily, so the assert earns its line.
verdicts.amendment:
## D5 Cell assignment and complex geometry

Every asset row carries `cell` = H3 res 8 of its point, built as **one more builder in `src/raincheck/ref.py` under `make ref`** — same Sedona write path and the same DuckDB `h3` oracle in `tests/test_ref.py` that ref/cells uses (with the `ST_ReducePrecision(g, 1e-9)` snap). No new module, no separate job.

Complex point = centroid of its constituent stations' gtfs lat/lon (496 station rows -> 445 complexes). The choice is cosmetic — the entrance-centroid alternative differs p50 26 m, p90 81 m, max 161 m, all well inside an H3-8 Cell — and the point is used only for the precip-Cell join and display, never for label attachment (D3).

Build gate: every asset's `cell` must exist in `ref/cells`; fail the build, never null it. `ref/cells` is `fullCover=false` (4,113 Cells fully inside the bbox; the 359 rim Cells are excluded), so a point near the bbox edge would otherwise get a Cell with no `cell_pixel` weights and join to zero precip in silence. Measured 2026-08-22: all 16,457 source points clear the nearest edge by 0.0164 deg vs an H3-8 span of ~0.0106 deg, so the gate passes clean today.

verdicts.reason: 'Frozen snapshot with frozen_at + per-source as-of dates' does not survive contact with the ref layer's own gate: build ticket 02 requires `make ref` twice to leave byte-identical tables, and ticket 02 solved exactly this by pinning aorc's frozen_at to the npz mtime and mrms's to a literal date. A wall-clock frozen_at, or a live SODA fetch at build time, breaks that gate on day one — the draft never says where the snapshot lives or that it is a file. The pick note is descriptive, not a rule: only one zip per feed exists on disk today (five at 2026-06-23, staten_island at 2026-07-28), the archiver adds one daily, and 'newest pick' would silently repartition the bus half of the registry on every rebuild. Provenance should be `pick_id` into the ref/picks table that already exists (7 rows, real MTA feed_versions) rather than a new date column or the draft's `feeds` string. Finally, the versioning has a hole that reaches 01: negatives are an anti-join against ref/assets, so a registry rebuild changes the negative class — but 01's `label_version = sha1(311 as-of, alert as-of, frozen thresholds, RADIUS_M)` has no assets term, and stale labels would silently look current. The v1 no-validity-windows call itself is right and stays.
verdicts.amendment:
## D6 Versioning and asset existence

`ref/assets` is frozen and must rebuild byte-identically (build ticket 02's ref gate). Sources are snapshotted to disk first and never fetched live at build, exactly like `archive/precip/aorc/coords.npz`: `data/archive/subway/i9wp-a4ja_2026-08-22.json` (assert 2,120 rows) and `data/archive/subway/39hk-dx4f_2026-08-22.json` (assert 496 rows), fetched only when missing. `src_asof` is the snapshot date literal, never `now()`.

Bus rows carry `pick_id` (FK to `ref/picks`, which already holds feed / published / feed_version / path). The six picks are **pinned by pick_id in the builder** — bronx, brooklyn, busco, manhattan, queens at 2026-06-23, staten_island at 2026-07-28 — not resolved as 'newest at build time': the archiver captures a zip a day and 'newest' makes the registry non-reproducible. The ~390 Transitland historical picks are deliberately unused in v1.

v1 scores the CURRENT asset universe; historical labels attach spatially, so an asset that opened mid-era (Second Av subway, 2017) inherits its location's earlier flood history — correct for exposure-of-the-location. No per-asset validity windows in v1; the asset-event anti-join negatives for events predating an asset are a known bias listed for 08's per-event diagnostics.

Because negatives are `ref/assets x flood_events` anti-joins, 01's label_version gains an assets term: `label_version = sha1(311 as-of, alert as-of, frozen thresholds, RADIUS_M, assets_src_asof)`. Rebuilding the registry invalidates gold/flood_labels by construction.

missing: Duplicate physical entrances. 2,120 rows are only 2,110 distinct coordinates: 9 coordinates carry 2-3 rows because one doorway serves two complexes (Fulton St / Chambers-WTC share 5 points, Wall St / Broad St share 2, the two 50 St stations share 1). The draft's uniqueness check was (complex_id, lat, lon), which cannot see this. Decide: keep one row per (complex, entrance) so both complexes inherit the doorway (recommended — D3 makes entrances feature carriers, so duplicate points cost nothing), and state that 07's DEM sampling and any entrance-grain diagnostic dedupe on geom, not on asset_id.

label_support has no legal value for a bus stop. 01's enum is {entrance, station, cell}; 13,370 bus stops attach by the same 100 m radius as entrances. Either rename to {radius, station, cell} (recommended, see D3) or add a bus value — but the draft picks neither, and 01 is already resolved, so 06 must own the propagation.

entry_allowed = NO. Measured (entry, exit): (YES,YES) 2,065, (NO,YES) 48, (YES,NO) 7. The 48 are exit-only stairs, physically identical holes in the sidewalk, so the rows stay — that is the answer, and the draft never gives it. Then decide whether either column survives: no consumer is named today (D3's open-stair count is entrance_type='Stair' regardless of direction), and carrying entry_allowed while dropping exit_allowed is arbitrary.

Borough. The draft carries no borough column and never says so. Note the premise is stale: as of 2026-08-22 all 66 SI entrance rows carry borough='SI' and all 21 SI station rows carry 'SI' — nothing to fix, no empty-borough rows exist in either dataset (entrances M 868 / B 580 / Q 355 / Bx 251 / SI 66; stations Bk 169 / M 153 / Q 83 / Bx 70 / SI 21). Decide explicitly: no borough column, derive from ref/cell_zone.borough via cell — and add the check that every asset's Cell is one of the 1,070 Cells with a zone (the other 3,043 are water/outside the taxi-zone layer), or borough is silently null for some assets.

Which snapshot, exactly, and where it lives. Dataset ids, host (data.ny.gov), as-of date, on-disk path, row-count assertions, and the fetch-only-when-missing rule. Without this the builder either calls SODA at build time (breaking the byte-identical ref gate) or invents a path.
Pick selection and rebuild policy. 'Newest pick per feed' vs pinned pick_ids, and what happens the day the archiver adds a 2026-08-23 zip — silently new bus stops, or an unchanged frozen table.

structure collapse. 9 of 445 complexes mix structures (608 Subway/Viaduct; 604, 606, 616, 621, 627, 630 Elevated+Subway; 615 Elevated/Open Cut; 626 Open Cut/Subway). No rule is given for the complex row's single value.

Whether ref/assets carries a name at all. 02's extractor already emits complex_ids so the alert join does not need names, but pipeline 14's serving panel, every map tooltip and every debug query do. If a name column exists, the 220 shared bus stop_ids with conflicting stop_names need the same min(feed) whole-row rule as the coordinates.

Does a registry rebuild invalidate gold/flood_labels? 01's label_version sha1 has no assets term while its negatives are a ref/assets anti-join, so today a re-frozen registry silently changes the negative class with no version change.

Physical layout of the table. One file or a partitioned directory, the sort key, and the byte-identical rebuild expectation. Every existing ref table is a single sorted part-00000.parquet moved from .staging/; ref/assets should say so rather than let a Spark default write N part files in nondeterministic order.

What the build does when an asset's H3 Cell is not in ref/cells — fail, drop with a count, or null the cell. Measured zero occurrences today, but the picks change weekly and a null cell means a silent zero-row precip join, not an error.

verdicts.reason: The column list cannot serve three of the four consumers. (a) NO station grain and NO gtfs_stop_id. 01's frozen attachment path is 'alert station -> GTFS stop_id -> complex_id -> entrances' and 02's delivered path is 'matched alias -> station rows -> complex_id, route-filtered via affected'. Both traverse the 496 station rows and their gtfs_stop_id/daytime_routes; the draft collapses 496->445 and keeps neither, so the join literally does not exist in ref/assets. 09's subway metric is per-station from subwaydata.nyc per-trip arrivals, which are keyed by GTFS stop -- also no join target. I verified the key is free and exact: /Users/ross/raincheck/research/flood-02-station-prototype/stations.json has 496 rows with station_id, complex_id, gtfs_stop_id, stop_name, daytime_routes, line, borough, structure; the local archive zip /Users/ross/raincheck/data/archive/static/subway/2026-08-07.zip has exactly 496 location_type=1 parent stops, and gtfs_stop_id joins them 496/496 with ZERO orphans both ways. (b) NO name column of any kind. 10's detector output and pipeline-14's panel must render 'likely flooding at X'; stop_name is present in every source already parsed (subway zip, all six bus zips). (c) `structure` is a PER-STATION field assigned to a complex row with no aggregation rule: 35 complexes hold >1 station (max 5) and 9 of them carry conflicting structure values (621 Broadway Junction Elevated+Subway, 626 Open Cut+Subway, 615 Elevated+Open Cut...). Elevated-vs-Subway is the single most predictive flood feature 08 could have, and D1 silently collapses it. (d) `cell` has no declared type; pipeline-09 conventions pin `cell` INT64 (ref/cells pk, gold/cell_hour_speed cell INT64, 'hex string at any JSON boundary'). A string h3 breaks every downstream join. (e) `feeds` as a pipe-list ignores ref/picks, whose pk is already pick_id = sha1 of the zip bytes.
verdicts.amendment: D1: `ref/assets` -- one GeoParquet 1.1 file, ~16,431 rows = 445 complexes + 496 stations + 2,120 entrances + 13,370 bus stops. Columns: asset_id, kind {complex, station, entrance, bus_stop}, name STRING (NOT NULL: stop_name for station/complex/bus_stop from GTFS stops.txt, street/corner for entrances), geom (POINT 4326), cell INT64 (H3 res 8, per pipeline-09 conventions; hex string only at JSON boundaries), complex_id (complex/station/entrance), station_id + gtfs_stop_id (station and entrance rows -- i9wp-a4ja carries both), parent_asset_id (station -> complex, entrance -> its station where known else its complex), structure (STATION rows only, from 39hk-dx4f; complexes do NOT carry it -- 9 complexes have conflicting values), daytime_routes + line (station rows), borough (station/complex from 39hk-dx4f, bus_stop via ref/cell_zone), entrance_type + entry_allowed (entrances), pick_id LIST<STRING> -> ref/picks (bus stops; replaces the `feeds` pipe-list). Cell-grain scoring still reads ref/cells directly. Build test: gtfs_stop_id joins the subway static pick's location_type=1 stops 496/496 with zero orphans (verified 2026-08-22).

verdicts.reason: `ent:<complex_id>:<sha1(lat3,lon)|8>` makes asset_id a function of the source coordinates, and asset_id is the ONLY join key two downstream tables use: gold/flood_labels (01) and 07's sampled elevation values. A re-geocode of i9wp-a4ja -- routine on Socrata -- silently mints new ids and orphans every label and every DEM/DSM sample, with no error anywhere. The rounding is also asymmetric and probably a typo: at NYC latitude 0.001 deg = 111 m, so lat3 discards real entrance separation while the un-rounded lon keeps full float noise; the hash is simultaneously lossy in one axis and jitter-sensitive in the other. Separately, the new station rows need a key, and station_id is a Socrata-internal number while gtfs_stop_id is source-native, verified unique across all 496, and the id every consumer (02, 09) already speaks.
verdicts.amendment: D2 Keys: complex `stn:<complex_id>` (445); station `sta:<gtfs_stop_id>` (496, e.g. sta:M01 -- source-native, verified unique and 1:1 against the GTFS parent stops); entrance `ent:<complex_id>:<sha1(lat,lon rounded to 5 dp BOTH)|8>` (~1 m quantum, symmetric); bus stop `bus:<stop_id>` (13,370; dedupe the 935 cross-feed shares by stop_id, coords from the lexicographically-first feed, all source pick_ids recorded). asset_id stability is a CONTRACT, not a hope: the frozen file is the key authority, and any rebuild must emit an added/removed/moved key-diff; a rebuild that orphans a row in gold/flood_labels or in 07's elevation table is a build failure, not a warning.

verdicts.reason: Three separate breaks. (a) It misstates the resolved upstream: 'alert labels land here [complex] per 02' is wrong -- 01's Answer routes station -> stop_id -> complex_id -> ENTRANCES with label_support='station', and 02 confirms 'entrances join on complex_id per 01'. Alert positives are entrance-grain rows; complexes have no alert channel at all. (b) Declaring bus_stop a published score unit silently multiplies 07's workload by ~7.5x: 07 budgets '~3 POSTs per epoch', which is exactly 2,120 entrances / ~1000 points per getSamples request -- entrances-only arithmetic. If bus stops are scored they need DEM+DSM too (13,370 more points, plus 445+496 subway rows), and 07 has not been told. (c) Measured on the real stop set: 13,370 bus stops occupy 1,035 res-8-equivalent cells -- mean 12.9 stops/cell, median 11, p90 26, max 67. Every cell-grain feature (precip from the pipeline-08 spine, 09's cell_hour_speed impact signal, cell-grain stormwater) is IDENTICAL across ~13 stops, and 01's 100 m radius paints near-identical 311 labels across them too. The only per-stop discriminator left is 07 elevation. So a 13,370-row bus-stop CSI is ~1,035 independent samples wearing a 13x multiplier -- exactly the kind of number 08's event-clustered errors are supposed to prevent. (d) The label channel differs by kind (entrances can receive alert labels; complexes and bus stops cannot), which 08's detectability anti-join must know and the registry never declares.
verdicts.amendment: D3 Scoring units, feature carriers, and label channels. Published score units: station (subway -- the grain 02/09 already speak), bus_stop, and Cell. Complex is a ROLLUP view over its stations/entrances (parent_asset_id), not a separately-modelled unit. Entrances are feature carriers and display detail; alert labels land on ENTRANCE rows with label_support='station' per 01, and roll up to station/complex by OR. The registry publishes, as a table not prose, which of 01's label sources can attach to each kind: 311/HWM/FloodNet/Sandy attach to every kind by 100 m radius or contains; alert-station labels attach to entrance rows ONLY. Elevation sampling universe = ALL asset rows (~16,431 points, ~17 getSamples POSTs per epoch at 1000 pts/request), not the 2,120 entrances 07 currently budgets -- flagged into 07. Effective resolution warning carried into 08: bus stops occupy only 1,035 distinct Cells (12.9 stops/cell, p90 26, max 67), so bus-stop-grain metrics must report the occupied-Cell count beside the asset count and cluster errors by Cell as well as by event.

verdicts.reason: No open consumer needs segment grain. 09's bus impact is cell-grain by construction (gold/cell_hour_speed is keyed cell INT64 x hour_end_utc x route_id x route_class -- there is no segment key to join to); 10 names its output grain as 'Cell + station'; 08's feature set is Cell-hour precip plus point-sampled elevation/stormwater; 07 samples points. The 311-attaches-identically rationale survives contact with all four. If anything the D3 measurement (12.9 bus stops per Cell) argues for FEWER units, not more. Keep the fog trigger as written.

The centroid is used as a real attachment target and it is a phantom location. 01's frozen rule says the 100 m geodesic radius is 'identical for every point source', so any complex POINT row in ref/assets becomes a 311/HWM/FloodNet attachment target. Measured on the 35 multi-station complexes (Socrata station list joined to the local GTFS parent-stop coords): the centroid sits up to 251 m from its own farthest station (p50 70 m), and for 2 complexes EVERY constituent station is more than 100 m from the centroid -- so at RADIUS_M=100 those complex rows attach reports from a spot with no station structure, and miss reports sitting on the actual platforms. 08's {50,100,200} m sweep makes the 50 m fold worse still. Separately, `cell` needs its INT64 type and a membership assertion: ref/cells is 4,113 hexes over the bbox (-74.30..-73.65, 40.45..40.95); any asset whose cell is absent from that set joins silver/precip_cell_hourly as NULL and drops out of scoring with no error. All NYC assets should fall inside, but 'should' is not a test.
verdicts.amendment: D5 Cell assignment and complex geometry. Every asset row carries cell INT64 = h3(point, res 8), built with the pipeline's existing tooling (Sedona writes, DuckDB h3 as test oracle). Build test, blocking: every asset cell is present in ref/cells (4,113 rows over the NYC bbox); the count of assets outside is reported and must be 0. Complex point = centroid of its constituent stations' GTFS lat/lon, for DISPLAY and the precip-cell join ONLY -- complexes and stations are NOT radius-attachment targets. Complex and station labels are inherited by OR over child entrance rows via parent_asset_id (measured justification: the centroid lies up to 251 m from its own stations, and 2 of the 35 multi-station complexes have no station within 100 m of their centroid). Entrances and bus stops keep their own points and are the only radius targets among the subway/bus kinds.

verdicts.reason: Three gaps. (a) The named bias example understates the real one by orders of magnitude: Second Av Subway is ~4 stations, while the registry applies a 2026-06/07 bus-stop snapshot to a 2010-2026 label era that contains the Bronx (2022) and Queens (2025) network redesigns -- bus stops are 81% of the asset universe and the churn is thousands of rows, so 08's anti-join negatives for pre-2022 events are dominated by stops that did not exist. (b) 01's label_version = sha1 of (311 as-of, alert as-of, frozen thresholds, RADIUS_M) does NOT include the asset registry, yet every row of gold/flood_labels is keyed by asset_id -- rebuild the registry and the labels change with an unchanged version string. (c) 07 explicitly asks where the sampled elevation values live and the draft never answers; and the per-feed provenance is recorded as loose dates when ref/picks already has the right key (pick_id = sha1 of the zip bytes). staten_island really is a different pick (2026-07-28 vs 2026-06-23 for the other five; subway static is 2026-08-07) -- verified in /Users/ross/raincheck/data/archive/static/.
verdicts.amendment: D6 Versioning and asset existence. ref/assets is a frozen, IMMUTABLE snapshot: consumers attach derived columns in siblings keyed by asset_id (07's DEM/DSM samples go to silver/asset_features, never as new columns here). Provenance: frozen_at, Socrata as-of per dataset (entrances i9wp-a4ja, stations 39hk-dx4f), and pick_id per bus feed from ref/picks -- five feeds on the 2026-06-23 pick, staten_island on 2026-07-28, subway static on 2026-08-07. Emit assets_version = sha1 over the sorted (asset_id, kind, lat, lon) tuples, and AMEND 01's label_version to include it, so a registry rebuild forces a label-version bump. v1 scores the current asset universe with no per-asset validity windows; the dominant bias is bus-stop churn, not subway openings -- the 2022 Bronx and 2025 Queens redesigns sit inside the label era and bus stops are 81% of the universe. 08 must therefore report a bus-stop sensitivity restricted to the post-redesign era beside the pooled number, and per-event diagnostics keep asset-kind as a reported dimension. Historical static picks exist back to ~2016 (Transitland + Wayback, with holes -- research/13-historic-gtfs-sources.md); add validity windows only if the diagnostics demand them.

missing: Station grain (496 rows) and gtfs_stop_id -- 09's subwaydata.nyc per-station delay join and 02's route-filtered alert path have NO join target in ref/assets as drafted. Verified free and exact: stations.json 496 rows join the local subway static pick's location_type=1 stops 496/496, zero orphans.

A human-readable `name` on every kind. 10's detector output ('areas and stations likely flooding') and pipeline-14's serving panel cannot label a single row. stop_name is present in the subway zip and all six bus zips already being parsed -- one field away.

borough, daytime_routes, line -- present in stations.json, dropped by the draft; needed for per-borough diagnostics in 08 and line-level subway delay attribution in 09. (No complex spans a borough: verified 0 of 445.)
`cell` column TYPE. Pipeline-09 pins cell INT64 (ref/cells pk, gold/cell_hour_speed cell INT64); the draft leaves it unstated, and a string h3 breaks 09's bus join and the precip spine join silently.

The rollup rule and the anti-join grain filter. 01's negative recipe is a literal `ref/assets x flood_events LEFT ANTI JOIN flood_labels` over the WHOLE table -- with mixed kinds that manufactures 445 x N complex negatives whose positive channel does not exist, and double-counts every flooded complex as 1 complex + k entrance rows. The registry must state: negatives are generated per kind, one score unit at a time, and parent labels = OR over children via parent_asset_id.

A per-kind label-channel table (which of 01's five label-grade sources can ever attach to which kind). 08's detectability anti-join is a binding obligation from 01 and cannot be built without it -- only entrance rows can ever receive an alert-station label.

Negative-universe BOUNDS, which 08's ticket asks for by name: |assets| x |events| stated per kind, plus the effective-independent-sample caveat (13,370 bus stops sit in only 1,035 Cells; measured mean 12.9/cell, median 11, p90 26, max 67).
assets_version hash, and the amendment to 01's label_version to include it -- otherwise a registry rebuild changes gold/flood_labels content with an unchanged version string.

Where 07's sampled elevation lands (sibling silver/asset_features keyed by asset_id; ref/assets immutable) AND the sampling universe size. 07's '~3 POSTs per epoch' is 2,120/1000 = entrances-only; D3's bus_stop score unit makes it ~16,431 points / ~17 POSTs per epoch.

pick_id per bus feed -> ref/picks (pk is already sha1 of the zip bytes). The draft records loose dates; staten_island is genuinely a different pick (2026-07-28 vs 2026-06-23), and the subway static pick (2026-08-07) is not mentioned at all.

structure at its natural grain. It is a per-station field; 9 of the 35 multi-station complexes carry conflicting values (Elevated+Subway, Open Cut+Subway, Elevated+Open Cut). Below-grade-vs-elevated is the strongest single flood feature available to 08 and the draft collapses it away.

Which kinds are radius-attachment targets versus inherit-only. 01's RADIUS_M rule is frozen and applies to every point row, so this must be settled in 06 or the complex centroids quietly become 311 attachment targets (measured: up to 251 m from their own stations).

The entrance -> station link (station_id / gtfs_stop_id on entrance rows, both present in i9wp-a4ja). Without it, an alert naming one station in a 5-station complex attaches to every entrance of the complex; with it, 08 can sweep station-precise versus complex-wide attachment as a fold-internal choice.

Reuse note the draft never makes: the bus-stop point set duplicates the pipeline's existing per-pick `stops` table (stop_id, stop_name, lon, lat, cell INT64, POINT geometry, partitioned by pick_id). Either read it or state why a separate derivation is needed.
